title: Bodies that settle disputes

match.reason: The bank card is mainly about consumer remedies (repair, replace, refund) and only touches NSW bodies in passing, whereas the new point teaches the range of Victorian bodies that settle disputes without a court, so it is a different idea and would need a new point.

draft.title: Bodies that settle disputes
card: Many civil disputes are settled by bodies outside the courts. These bodies are usually quicker, cheaper and less formal than a court.
a body that hears both sides and makes a decision. The Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (VCAT) hears matters such as tenancy and building disputes.
a body that investigates complaints about the actions of an organisation, such as a government department. It looks into the complaint and does not act as a judge.
a body such as Consumer Affairs Victoria that gives information about consumer and tenancy rights and can help the parties reach agreement. It is not a court.
draft.remember: Tribunals decide, ombudsmen investigate and complaints bodies inform and assist, all without going to court.

a.q: Which description best fits the role of VCAT?
opts: It hears both sides and decides tenancy disputes
It investigates complaints about a government department
It gives consumers information and helps parties agree
It hears the largest civil claims in front of a jury
a.why: VCAT is a tribunal, so it hears both sides and makes a decision. Investigating complaints is the role of an ombudsman, and giving information and help is what a body such as Consumer Affairs Victoria does.
a.clue: A tribunal is the body that makes a decision.

b.q: Priya believes her energy provider billed her wrongly. She wants her complaint investigated, not a judge's ruling. Which body suits her aim best?
b.why: An ombudsman investigates complaints about the actions of an organisation, which is what Priya wants. VCAT is tempting because it settles disputes, but it hears both sides and decides, and the courts are formal and not needed here.
b.clue: Which body looks into complaints rather than deciding like a judge?

a.best: It hears both sides and decides tenancy disputes

check.summary: No problems found. The roles of VCAT, ombudsmen and Consumer Affairs Victoria are accurate, and each question has a single defensible answer.
